title: Slate onboarding conductor: streamlined intake, conversion, pinning, and metricization
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: Deliver an end-to-end conductor that takes community weights through acceptance gates (sanity + deterministic conversion), produces a runtime-ready artifact, pins a canonical version, and publishes a lightweight performance profile into the catalog. This ticket implements the orchestration, failure semantics, and telemetry hooks needed for deterministic, auditable onboarding runs that support fast operator triage and automated rollouts.

Background: Current intake path is fragmented: ad-hoc conversions, manual pin recommendations, and inconsistent smoke coverage. That produces variance in runtime performance claims and slows model publication. We need a resilient, observable pipeline that enforces deterministic conversion steps, captures per-step artifacts, and surfaces metrics that feed the public profile publish step.

Scope and deliverables:
- Orchestrator service that sequences intake -> conversion -> deterministic validation -> profile benchmark -> pin decision -> publish.
- Conversion runner that produces reproducible runtime bundles with canonical metadata and checksums.
- Deterministic smoke suite (sanity prompts, memory/latency microbench) with pass/fail thresholds.
- Pin recommendation engine that emits a recommended pin and rationale (latency/cost/quality tradeoffs) to be reviewed or auto-approved per policy.
- Profile publisher that writes performance metadata to the model catalog and triggers console indexing.
- Telemetry and trace spans for each stage; failure hooks to capture artifacts and auto-create triage issues when certain classes of failures occur.
proposal:
Implement a stateful conductor (Kubernetes jobs + a lightweight controller) that owns a single-run CRD-like document for each intake. Each stage emits an indexable artifact (logs, checksums, perf CSV). Use existing conversion binaries (weights-convert v2) and wrap them with deterministic seeds, pinned tool versions, and content-addressed outputs. For profile metrics we run a short micro-benchmark harness with representative prompt families (completion, chat, long-context) using sampled inputs from our corpus. The pin recommendation uses a weighted scoring function: latency (40%), memory footprint (20%), token cost (20%), and quality (20%) based on evals. Manual intervention allowed for high-risk models.

Trade-offs: Full end-to-end benchmarking is expensive; we intentionally limit the initial profile to 1-2 representative lengths and a 30-sample quality check to balance cost vs. signal. Auto-approval policy defaults to false for models with any safety flags.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag behind onboarding-slate; 2) Canary runs on internal sandbox with synthetic manifests; 3) Shadow run against a subset of community uploads for 2 weeks; 4) Gradual promotion to default flow and catalog publish.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor accepts a manifest and creates a single canonical run record with lifecycle states
Conversion step produces content-addressed runtime bundle with checksum and tool_version metadata
Deterministic smoke suite runs automatically and reports pass/fail with artifacts in storage
Pin recommendation is generated and stored; policy gate either auto-approves or creates a review task
Performance profile JSON with latency, mem, and token-cost estimates is published to model catalog path
End-to-end telemetry and traces exist; failures generate triage issues with links to logs and bundles
